blocks.text: Oxidation of organic compounds involving reaction with oxygen is usually the combustion reaction:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Combustion gives water, not hydrogen, and the printed equation is not balanced. The balanced equation is C₂H₆ + 7/2 O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O (or 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O).
Reactions of organic compounds with oxidizing agents.e.g.
i) Ozonolysis is a method of oxidatively cleaving alkenes using ozone (O₃).

blocks.alt: 1-Propene, H3C-CH=CH2, with O3 gives the ozonide ring; Zn/H2O gives acetaldehyde (H3C-CHO) + formaldehyde (HCHO), which are reduced to ethanol, H3C-CH2-OH, and methanol, CH3-OH.
blocks.caption: i) Ozonolysis of propene (original drawing after the scheme printed on p268 of the textbook).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed scheme shows the formation of the ozonide with a reversible arrow; it is a one-way reaction, drawn above with a single arrow.
ii) The epoxidation of alkene is also example of oxidation reaction. In this reaction various oxidizing agents can be used like molecular oxygen and metal catalysts.

blocks.alt: An alkene (H2C=CH2) + O2 gives the epoxide (a three-membered ring of two carbons and one O), which with H+/H2O gives ethane-1,2-diol.
blocks.caption: ii) Epoxidation of an alkene (original drawing after the scheme printed on p268 of the textbook).

blocks.text: iv) Reaction of primary alcohols with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ to make carboxylic acids, detail will be discussed in class 12 syllabus.
Addition of hydrogen to carbon-carbon double bond to form alkane is an example of organic reduction reaction.

Various reducing agents are used in Organic synthesis. e.g; LiAlH₄, NaBH₄, Sn + conc.HCl. Reduction of nitriles to amines, amides to amines, carboxylic acid to primary alcohols, nitrobenzene to phenylamine are all examples of reduction and will be studied in class 12 syllabus.
